status: Four journal semantic-purge cases pass through final retirement, recovery, reclamation and continued writer use. Production is unchanged. Issue remains open until merge.

diagnosis.result: Rollback returns the exact publication error while the physical release injection remains armed; transaction close later returns the exact release error; fixture disposal masks both with a closed-journal drain.
mechanism: The native transaction base owns the old snapshot pin. Candidate reader close does not retire that base. Transaction close awaits readers, candidate, then base; base awaits snapshot close, which closes formats, dump and compensation resources.

Rollback publication fails after reserving the old image. Compensation queues the image release in the durable rel state while the old base pin is live. Its drain cannot release that image yet, so rollback returns the original publication Error alone.

Final pin close releases the version and invokes JournalMediaPins.afterReaderRelease. Its retirement Promise awaits the serialized release-gate drain. The injected physical store release fails there, not during rollback. This Promise is observed by awaited transaction retirement; no lost production callback is demonstrated.

The old assertion expected both errors during rollback. When it failed, final transaction close threw the deferred release error. Outer fixture disposal began closing the journal before ownership releaseAll drained the remaining queue, producing the misleading closed-journal error.

The test now preserves publication and physical release Errors at their real boundaries using the existing releaseRead aggregation contract. After the one-shot external release failure it verifies every pin is gone and durable head is behind tail, then performs one explicit owner releaseAll recovery before disposal and checks head reaches that saved tail.

Fixture teardown releases ownership before journal disposal, attempts every resource cleanup, and reports the original action Error followed by cleanup Errors through historyMutationFailure. It no longer disables an armed release injection during cleanup.

finalRegression.terminalAssertions: Each case validates candidate transformation, persisted primary/mirror and frontier after publication/rollback, exact on-disk owner digest sets, immutable readable base, verified original blob bytes, zero pre-retirement reclamation, awaited retirement, zero live rows/bytes, unchanged 440-row/8MiB ownership bounds, no final reservations, two reclaimed objects and successful subsequent add/read/persist while history remains alive.
finalRegression.fourth: A physical release barrier holds the real store release. Close must stay pending until resumed. The observed AggregateError contains exactly the original publication Error and physical release Error in that order and by identity. Durable recovery occurs only after that expected failure has been asserted.

checks: Single action failure is the same Error.
Single physical cleanup failure is the same Error.
Action plus cleanup errors preserve exact identity, order and original cause.

No prior production receipt is invalidated. Earlier pending-media, no-file, queue and reader results are nevertheless refreshed here. Other HTTP/oracle receipts are source-matched historical evidence, not new runs. Full native memory acceptance remains pending; the original tools timeout is not promoted or retried.

controlQualifications: All three verified production mutations restore by cmp and SHA256 against saved bytes and HEAD before positive gates.
Early drain fails exact owner predicates and pre-close reclamation. It does not establish execution of assertions after the first failing predicate in a case.
The unobserved-retirement mutation fails final owner-release assertions; its fourth physical error alone is not counted as an independent matcher.

The supplementary ignored-retirement mutant attaches rejection observers only to discarded mutant cleanup promises. That prevents its deliberately dropped physical failure from masking the held-release barrier matcher: expected unsettled false, observed true. No such catch exists in production or the passing fixture.
Ignored durable head acknowledgement fails a persisted-head matcher and the exact injected write-error rejection. Its unhandled error is separately recorded, not counted as matcher sensitivity.
Restoring the original fixture fails both new cleanup-error assertions. Current fixture bytes restore by cmp and SHA256; subsequent complete journal and fixture files pass.
